findings.title: Retained credit reads clone the live Account principal as structured data

evidence.detail: VerifiedPrincipal permits currentAssertion, a function used for live authority revalidation.
AccountAssertionVerifier.verify returns that function as an enumerable own property for verified Account principals.

openRetainedCreditAssociationRead immediately calls structuredClone(principal). A function-valued property cannot be structured-cloned, so this is expected to throw DataCloneError before any activation/read work.

The basis retains reader: VerifiedPrincipal. The same class recurs in basis/input/owner-argument cloning at lines 234, 240, 250, 264, 283, 415, 472, 555, 593, 600, 611, 622, 666 and 673; changing only the first clone would not support a live principal throughout the read.
The reader fixture contains only issuer and subject, so existing owner tests do not exercise the Account-issued shape.
The existing session separates cursor identity from currentAssertion and expiry while retaining live request verification.

findings.expectedImpact: When a consumer passes the actual Account-verified principal into this owner, opening the retained credit read is expected to fail, preventing its collection or witness read. No installed public consumer or public HTTP failure was demonstrated by this review.

findings.recommendation: Owner should separate serializable continuation identity from the live principal, retain currentAssertion for authority/disclosure revalidation, and exercise open/fence/page/witness paths using the real Account-issued principal shape.
